newsitem.title: CHILE: Profit-take drags down Chilean shrs, mkt ends mixed.
newsitem.headline: Profit-take drags down Chilean shrs, mkt ends mixed.

text.p: Chilean blue chips fell in afternoon trade as investors skimmed off profits from the bolsa's recent gains, with most of the stars of the recent rally retreating.
Brokers, citing Wall Street's surge, said they expected the Santiago Stock Exchange to resume its bullish trend next week despite what they considered a technical retreat.

The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares ended 0.67 percent lower at 136.14 points. The general IGPA index was almost unchanged, ending 0.03 percent higher at 5843.79 points on strong volume of 18.8 billion pesos.
"This was a typical technical correction," said one broker. "We went up too fast this week, and the air went out of the market," said another.
Others cited a slight drop in copper prices for a tempering of the market's euphoria.
Some of the big gainers of the recent rally, including electrical companies Endesa, Enersis and Chilgener, posted modest declines.
Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile A series slipped 2.1 percent to 3,690 pesos after a strong run-up this week, partly on expectations of its planned merger with long-distance rival VTR.

The Luksic group, owners of VTR, had problems with their planned stock placement for Quinenco, the holding company for the group's vast financial and industrial interests, after stock regulators ordered it to suspend the initial public offering for publishing a newspaper ad announcing the IPO prematurely.
Quinenco later said the IPO would go ahead as planned anyway, but regulators could not be reached for comment and the IPO's status was not entirely clear by the time the market closed.
Paper pulp makers were among the few big-volume gainers.

Copec rose 1.7 percent to 1995 pesos on reports of higher pulp prices and a Santander Investment report raising estimates for 1997 earnings-per-share, a broker said. Copec's competitor CMPC rose one percent to 5,000 pesos, following an upgrade to buy from hold by ING Barings.

Banmedica rose 4.4 percent to 188 pesos following its purchase with Cruz Blanca of 50 percent of Consorcio Nacional de Seguros from Bankers Trust, and Maderas y Sinteticos (Masisa) was up 1.8 percent to 223 pesos.
